        The Charlotte Hornets will retire the No. 1 jersey of Muggsy Bogues on Feb. 11, the team announced Tuesday. Bogues, at 5-foot-3, is the shortest player in NBA history, and now that the Hornets will hang his jersey in the rafters of the Spectrum Center, he will become, by a wide margin, the shortest player in NBA history to have his jersey retired. That distinction was previously held by Calvin Murphy, the 5-foot-9 point guard who played his entire career for the San Diego and later Houston Rockets.Bogues, a college star at Wake Forest, was drafted No. 12 overall by the Washington Bullets in 1987. That allowed him to start his career playing next to the 7-foot-7 Manute Bol, who, at the time, was the tallest player in NBA history (a title he now shares with Gheorghe Mureșan). However, the Bullets left Bogues unprotected in the 1988 expansion draft, which allowed the incoming Charlotte Hornets to swipe him before their inaugural season.
Washington's loss was Charlotte's gain. Bogues grew into the full-time starting point guard for the Hornets during the 1989-90 season and held his post through 1997. He never made an All-Star Team or averaged more than 11.1 points per game, but he averaged double-digit assists on multiple occasions and is Charlotte's all-time leader in steals. The 90s represent the most successful era in Hornets history, with Bogues, Larry Johnson and Alonzo Mourning leading Charlotte to several postseason trips.Now, aside from his distinction as the NBA's shortest player ever, Bogues is remembered fondly for his role in Space Jam. He was one of the five then-active NBA players whose talent was stolen by the MonStars to face Michael Jordan and the Looney Tunes. 
Bogues will become the third member of the Hornets to have his jersey retired, joining former teammates Bobby Phills, who died in a car accident in 2000, and Dell Curry, who remains with the team as a broadcaster.

That means it's time to give out Attacking Third Team of the Week honors.After weekly matches across the 2026 NWSL season, Attacking Third analysts will select players, a head coach, and an honorary captain based on weekend performances. Here you can find a mix of stats and data, analysis from our pundits, and highlights you may have missed over the weekend. If you're keeping track of who earned past honors, check out our previous team of the week.It's been a wild year, and it feels like it's just getting started now that the postseason is rapidly approaching. That also means our team of the week honors will look slightly different following games moving forward. We'll hand out one more set of honors after Decision Day on November 1, but afterward, we'll be locked into playoffs and performances from the quarterfinals onward. Here's who made the latest edition:Goalkeeper: Ann-Katrin Berger (Gotham FC)When it comes to the NWSL Shield, Gotham FC is taking the long road. If they manage to lift it, it'll be because they have a great goalkeeper to keep away any spoilers. Ann-Katrin Berger is back on the team of the week honors for keeping a newly eliminated and motivated Orlando Pride from deterring Gotham's quest for the title. She faced 19 shots, eight attempts on target, and made seven saves in a narrow but crucial victory. 
Defender: Evelyn Shores (Angel City FC)Angel City's Evelyn Shores has become a bona fide two-way player this season and stands out on a backline that has Sarah Gorden and Savy King. She's back on the team of the week for another stellar performance, where she was instrumental in building up play and keeping the backline in shape. She led defenders on the team in duels (seven) and co-led in clearances (two) and interceptions (two). Defender: Tierna Davidson (Gotham FC)Not that Tierna Davidson needed any more bullet points on her long resume for NWSL defender of the year, but scoring headers in the box was already on there. She did it again for Gotham FC and scored a decisive game-winner to keep the club ahead in the NWSL Shield race
Defender: Kaleigh Kurtz (Denver Summit)If you've ever heard of the iron woman concept in NWSL, then you're already familiar with Kaleigh Kurtz, but you might not be familiar with her dance moves. She showed them off after scoring her first goal with Denver Summit.
Defender: Janine Sonis (Denver Summit)Back on the team of the week is Janine Sonis after a two-assist performance for Denver Summit in a must-win game. Denver's playoff destiny is tricky, but possible, and Sonis is making sure she's leaving with something, her seventh and eighth assists of the year.
Midfielder: Jessie Fleming (Portland Thorns)When the going gets tough this season, the tough runs away in fear of Jessie Fleming. The defensive midfielder has stepped up the club in a massive way between roster injuries and a red card suspension for Sophia Wilson. The Canadian international co-led the team in touches (66), led the team in recoveries (eight), and was a frequent outlet in building up play in a massive win over North Carolina.Midfielder: Alba Caño (Boston Legacy)Boston Legacy midfielder Alba Caño helped keep the team's spoiler reputation alive with an equalizer against San Diego. No NWSL Shield claimed on Boston's watch.
Midfielder: Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current)In 2024, Croix Bethune matched a single-season assist record (10) as a rookie. Now, it solely belongs to her. She delivered the record-setting assist to Vanessa DiBernardo for the game-winner.
Forward: Natasha Flint (Denver Summit)Seems like three points are easy to nab when Natasha Flint scores a break. The three points and goal differential could prove big in the playoff push.
Forward: Gisele Thompson (Angel City FC)Flexing her versatility over the weekend was Gisele Thompson for Angel City. Took her time on the ball and nailed the clinical finish.
Forward: Marie Muller (Portland Thorns FC)Portland Thorns are a club with a lot of history, and Marie Muller etched her name into the chapter of big moments. A lethal blast on goal clinched a playoff spot for the team.
Coach: Leif Gunnar Smerud (Angel City FC)The head-coaching rumor mill has gone pretty silent after Angel City's impressive second-half run under interim manager Leif Smerud. Another three points at home and the club is back in the playoffs for the first time since 2023. The performance is going to make it difficult for the front office to move on from the interim magician. Honorary captain: Portland's dream-making goalIt wasn't just Portland Thorns thanking Marie Muller for her game-winning goal, but several others. Not quite decision day, but it was a defining goal for several clubs. The game-winner clinched playoff spots for Portland, Kansas City Current, Utah Royals, and Angel City FC.

The second driver is a contender but is unlikely to win in the eyes of oddsmakers, but you'd win $200 after risking $100 if he does indeed pull off the upset.When you can bet on motor sports oddsThe racing schedule varies across NASCAR, F1 and IndyCar but there are usually weekly races with occasional breaks. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event.         After a few false starts, the coaching carousel finally started spinning in late October.It's not surprising the silly season is off to a slow start after 2025's record-breaking churn. The FBS hired 32 new head coaches, including 17 in the four power conferences, and hundreds more assistant coaches changed jobs.Ninety-three FBS programs have changed coaches over the last three offseasons. The question is whether we've hit a cooling period as schools wrestle with the challenging economics of the NIL and revenue-sharing era. Maryland kicked off the firing season Oct. 21. More power programs have followed. CBS Sports is tracking every move in the 2026-27 cycle and grading each hire below.Power Four
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Baylor -- OUT: Dave Aranda | IN: TBD
Dave Aranda won a Big 12 title in 2021 but otherwise led the Bears with middling success over seven seasons. He finished 40-40 and was below .500 in the Big 12 (26-32). Don't be surprised if Baylor seeks an offensive coach, particularly one with strong connections to the Texas high school scene. UTSA's Jeff Traylor, Texas State's GJ Kinne and USC's Lincoln Riley are strong candidates to consider in Waco.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Maryland -- OUT: Mike Locksley | IN: TBDMaryland kicked off the coaching carousel this year. Mike Locksley is out halfway through his eighth season at Maryland, where he was 39-54 overall. The Terps were 4-8 in back-to-back seasons leading to the decisive 2026. A wide variety of candidates will be considered in College Park. Wake Forest's Jake Dickert, a popular name elsewhere, and Memphis' Charles Huff, a Maryland native, immediately come to mind. The Terps have better NIL resources than a year ago, but the job is still difficult in the Big Ten.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    NC State -- OUT: Dave Doeren | IN: TBD
Dave Doeren is out after 14 years in Raleigh, following a disappointing 31-28 loss at Stanford that dropped the Wolfpack to 1-3 in the ACC. Doeren seemed just good enough to win seven to nine games every year, but disappointing losses always railroaded what could have been special seasons. A downtick in success over the last three years made it clear a change was needed. The candidate with the most heat is legendary NC State quarterback Philip Rivers. He's coached high school football for five years in Alabama and interviewed for the Buffalo Bills' job in January. His son, Gunner, is committed to NC State. This job has a wide variety of potential candidates, including Miami offensive coordinator Shannon Dawson, UNLV's Dan Mullen and Memphis' Charles Huff.

How to bet on horse racing: Most popular types of wagers There are a plethora of different wagering options available on each race. We will go through the three traditional bets – Win, Place and Show – as well as the combinations of each. Below are horse racing betting tips that identify bet types and the differences between the odds found at sportsbook and racing odds.  Each horse will have different odds for each bet type. These odds let you know the horse's expected return on each individual bet type. It's important to note that the odds on each horse fluctuate constantly and payouts are calculated based on the final odds, not the exact odds from the time you place your bet, a major difference from betting on other sports.               Differences in horse racing odds vs. sportsbook odds             Horse racing odds rely on pari-mutuel wagering, which is a system that pools together all of the money bet on each market up until the race begins. The track and the books take a certain percentage or rake for their operations (the Takeout), and the remainder of the pool is then divided among the winning ticket holders. The takeout is divided between the house (track) and horsemen, including race purses.               What is particularly unique about this system for those who are accustomed to betting on sports is that your odds can shift after you place the bet until they lock when the race begins. On sports betting apps, if you bet something at 10-1 and it later moves to 8-1, you still receive the 10-1 payout. In horse racing, your payout will change based on the way the market moves to create the final odds. The final odds you'll receive are determined by how much is bet on each horse and the Takeout.              The standard horse racing unit for win, place, or show bets is $2.                         Win             The win bet is simply betting on which horse will come in first place. Using the 2026 Herbie Dyke Stakes as an example, the winner was Legarto and finished with 12-5 odds. A $2 Win bet paid $6.80, a product of the standard $4.80 for a 12-5 payout on a $2 bet, plus your original $2 wager amount back.                          Place             The Place bet allows you to wager on whether a horse will finish first or second in a race, meaning two Place bets will pay out on each race. This gives you a greater chance of winning, but lowers your odds on the horse if they place.              Using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as the example again, a $2 Place bet on the No. 18 horse only returned $7.50 compared to the $17.96 for a Win bet. But also, a $2 Place bet on the No. 8 horse (Journalism), who was the favorite but came in second, paid $4.94 while the Win bet lost.                           Show             A Show bet is a highly conservative betting option. You are wagering on whether a horse will finish in the top three positions. That means three Show bets will pay out each race. For example, a $2 Show bet on a 10-1 winner returned $4. As one might expect, show bet odds are far less favorable than win bet odds, making them one of the more conservative wagers available in horse racing.                           Win/Place             Additionally, you can combine these bets on each horse when you're placing your wagers. That means if you want to bet on a horse to win and place, you can do that. A $2 Win/Place bet really means you're betting $4 – a $2 Win bet and a $2 Place bet. If the horse you bet on wins, you will win both bets. If the horse finishes second, you would only win the Place bet.                           Place/Show             The same is available for a Place/Show bet, where a $2 Place/Show bet would be $4 wagered on a $2 Place bet and a $2 Show bet. If your horse finishes first or second, you would win both, but if it finishes third, you would only win the Show bet.                           Win/Place/Show (Across The Board)              Lastly, you can bet on all three options in what is often referred to as an Across The Board bet. A $2 Across The Board bet would really be $6 wagered – $2 on Win, $2 on Place, and $2 on Show. If you make an Across The Board bet and your horse wins, you pay out on all three wagers.              It's important to note that betting on Win/Place/Show combinations may not result in a net return even if one of the bets pays. For example, at the 2024 Kentucky Derby, an Across The Board bet on the 11 horse would've returned just $5.58 on $6 wagered.                           The most popular horse racing bet types             Many horse racing bettors place exotic bets to try to predict where multiple horses will finish in a race. These combination wagers offer the chance for bigger payouts, but come with a lower probability of winning (just like same game parlays in sports betting).              It is important to note that, unlike sports betting, there is no standard odds calculation to use for determining exotic payouts. Because of parimutuel wagering, odds can fluctuate until the race begins based on which horses are taking the most action. Additionally, live horse racing betting is available, adding another layer of entertainment for those watching races as they take place.               Exactas             An exacta bet in horse racing functions the same as it does across other sports. The bettor must pick the exact finishing order. For example, if someone wants to place an exacta bet with two horses, they must select each horse and where it will finish exactly. Once again using the 2025 Kentucky Derby as an example, a $2 exacta on the No. 18 and No. 8 horses (who closed with final odds of 7-1 and almost 3-1) paid $48.32. This style of betting can be seen in plenty of other sports, especially in futures betting.  Exotics winnings will vary based on the number of horses in the race, the odds of the top-finishing horses, and the size of the pool. For example, the field for the 2024 Kentucky Derby saw a longer shot horse win, so the exacta pool paid $258.56 -- significantly more than the 2025 Derby.                           Trifectas             This horse racing wager is placing a bet on the exact order of the top-three finishers in a race. A straight trifecta will pay handsomely, but is extremely difficult to hit. Trifecta payouts are often shown for $0.50 bets, but some will show for $1 bets as well. The payout screen will tell you which, but that's important to note so you're aware of how much you are getting back.              The 2025 Kentucky Derby Trifecta paid $231.12 on a $1 Trifecta bet.                           Superfectas             Superfecta bets try to predict the exact order of the top-four finishers in a horse race. The superfecta payout is usually shown for a $1 bet. For the 2025 Kentucky Derby, a $1 superfecta that added the fourth-place No. 3 horse to the trifecta paid $1,682.27.                          Super High 5             Some books will allow you to bet on the top-five finishers in their exact order in what is called a Super High 5 bet. Those payouts will again be shown for a $1 wager. The odds of hitting a Super High 5, especially in a large field race, are exceptionally low. They are equivalent to multi-leg futures parlays in sports betting.  The 2025 Kentucky Derby's $1 Super High Five paid $38,405.96.                          Box             A box bet allows you to have every possible combination for exotics. If you think you know which two horses will hit the exacta but are not sure of their specific order, you can box it. The same goes for trifectas and superfectas. The more horses you box together, the lower your total profits on the payout will be.              For example, a three-horse exacta box bet costs $12 to bet, as you are betting $2 on all six potential combinations between those three horses:             $2 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 3 second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 3 in first and No. 2 in second$2 on No. 2 in first and No. 1 in second$2 on No. 1 in first and No. 3 in secondYou can do the same for Trifectas and Superfectas, but at exponentially escalating costs. A $1 Trifecta Box with three horses is six combinations, so $6 wagered:             $1 on No. 1 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 1 in first, No. 3 in second, No. 2 in first$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 3 in third$1 on No. 2 in first, No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 1 in second, No. 2 in third$1 on No. 3 in first, No. 2 in second, No. 1 in firstFrom there, four horses in a $1 trifecta box is 24 combinations for $24 wagered. Five horses make 60 possible combinations for $60.              A $1 Superfecta box of four horses is $24 wagered, five horses is $120 wagered and six horses is $360 wagered.                           How to bet on horse racing: Multi-race wagers             While those exotics offer a variety of options for betting on individual races, you can also bet on multiple races at the same track in various ways. These combination wagers pay out based on the betting pool, allowing you to choose a handful of horses you're confident in throughout the day to increase your potential payout.                           Daily Double             The Daily Double is exactly what it sounds like: Betting on back-to-back race winners from that day. The odds for Daily Doubles vary based on the odds for the individual horses you bet and the overall Daily Double betting pool. As an example, the $2 Daily Double at Horseshoe Indianapolis on April 15, 2025 from the first two races with the 7 horse in the first race (went off at 1-1 odds) and the 4 horse in the second race (went off at 3-5 odds) paid $8.              Once the first race ends, the payouts for each potential Daily Double will be shown under a "Will Pays" tab on the next race's betting screen.                           Pick-3, Pick-4, Pick-5 and Pick-6             Along with the Daily Double, there are more options for betting the winner of multiple races in a row at the same track. The Pick-3 is picking the winner in three consecutive races, the Pick-4 in four consecutive races, and so on for the Pick-5 and Pick-6.             Like exotics, the pool amount and the odds for each horse wagered on determine the payouts for these multi-race wagers. The default unit for these bets varies from book to book, with FanDuel showing $0.50 payouts and TwinSpires showing $1 payouts in the Will Pays section.              The more races you put together on a ticket, the more you can win. But as with any multi-race wager, the more legs you add, the harder it is to win. In this way, these bets function similarly to parlays in other sports.  For some of the biggest races, the Pick-6 will feature a set guaranteed prize pool for the winner(s) no matter what the actual wagered amount is. The 2024 Kentucky Derby featured a $1 million guaranteed pool on TwinSpires for Pick-6s on races 6 through 11 at Churchill Downs.                           Understanding horse racing payouts             After the race, the winning payouts will be displayed for each bet type. The standard unit for win/place/show and exactas is a $2 bet. Trifectas, superfectas and super high 5s are typically shown as $1 or $0.50, but will say explicitly which on the payout board.              The payouts for each horse in the top three for the 2025 Kentucky Derby looked as follows:             2025 Kentucky DerbyWinPlaceShowSovereignty (No. 18) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$17.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$7.50 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$5.58 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Journalism (No. 8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             $4.94 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$3.70 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				Baeza (No. 21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 								             				             $8.38 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				             If you bet more (or less) than the standard $2 unit, you multiply the payout by how much you bet and divide by the standard unit. For example, a $10 Win bet on Sovereignty returned $89.80, while a $25 Show bet on Journalism would've returned $46.25.              For the single-race exotics at the 2025 Kentucky Derby, the payouts were as follows:              2025 Kentucky DerbyPayout$2 Exacta (18-8) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$48.32 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Trifecta (18-8-21) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$231.12 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Superfecta (18-8-21-3) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1,682.27 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$1 Super High 5 (18-8-21-3-20) 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				$38,405.96 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				 				            Biggest horse races beyond Kentucky Derby betting            The horse racing calendar operates year-round, but there are six events on the schedule that serve as the most important, thus attracting the best fields. The three Triple Crown events headline for the general public, but the Breeders' Cup, Pegasus World Cup and Dubai World Cup all offer massive purses and attract some of the best horses and fields in all of racing.             October 30-31, 2026: Breeders' Cup January 23, 2027: Pegasus World CupMarch 27, 2027: Dubai World CupMay 1, 2027: Kentucky DerbyMay 15, 2027: Preakness StakesJune 5, 2027: Belmont Stakes             Triple Crown of horse racing             The Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes make up horse racing's Triple Crown. There are 13 horses that have completed the Triple Crown, winning all three events, and only two – American Pharoah (2015) and Justify (2018) – have accomplished that feat in the 21st century.              Not every horse competes in all three Triple Crown events. Each race operates at different lengths, and the turnaround time can be too quick for trainers to be comfortable running their horse in one after the other. Some Derby winners don't run the Preakness, while some have made it two legs before withdrawing from the Belmont.              The Kentucky Derby is a 1 1/4 mile race, the Preakness Stakes is 1 3/16 mile, and the Belmont Stakes is a grueling 1 1/2 mile event (although it is being run currently at 1 1/4 mile at Saratoga Race Course due to renovations at Belmont Park).                           Tips and advice for betting on horse racing             There are a number of strategies for betting on horse racing, but it all starts with understanding the horses and knowing their strengths, weaknesses and past performances.                           Racing forms and past performances             Racing forms are race-day publications and programs available at tracks and online to preview the day's races at each track. They are full of data and information from past races. All of the best horse racing betting apps have integrated much of this information into their betting screen.                           Track conditions             Before you even get to the horses, understanding track conditions is vital. Knowing if a track is dirt or grass, firm and fast or soft and slow, is critical information to know so you can look at which horses in a given race run best in certain conditions.                           Horse tendencies              From there, you want to understand the tendencies of horses in the field. Some horses get out to fast starts and try to push the pace, while others hang back and try to make a late kick. If most of the field is expected to push the pace and run it fast, then a horse that prefers to stay back may be at an advantage due to its advantage in a late-game run.              The opposite could be true, too; if the pace is going to be slower early, frontrunners are more likely to hold their position. Some of this information can be found in PPs or Past Performance data.                           Post position             Post position can also matter to a horse's success. Some prefer to run the rail (on the inside of the track) while others prefer being on the outside and running with more space around them. This information is all worth considering and comparing with the other horses in the field.                          Trainer and jockey information             A horse's trainer and jockey will also have tendencies. Some trainers are better at getting horses ready for a certain type of track, but maybe don't have a great track record at others. Some jockeys may be more or less aggressive on the track, which may or may not work well with that specific horse's tendencies, or they may have a long track record with that horse and know how to get the most out of them.                           Workout times             There's also plenty of data available that can help you. Workout times, if available, can give you an idea of how a horse has been running in training before a big race.                           Speed figures             Speed figures are like advanced stats of the horse racing world, offering a metric to show how well a horse has been running in its recent races that factors in things like field strength and track quality.              Taking all of that data into account is important to betting on horse racing, and for beginners it's best to ease in and do as much observing as you do betting. You'll start to find certain trends for horses, jockeys, trainers and tracks that can help you find edges on the odds board going forward.                          Manage your horse racing betting bankroll             Managing your bankroll with what percentage of money you have set aside for horse racing betting is vital to increasing your chances of scoring big at some point. Just like in sports betting, where most bankroll management experts advise no more than 2% of your bankroll should be bet on any given game, the same principle can be applied to any given horse race.                           Rules and responsible gaming             Responsible gambling is taken very seriously across all racebooks. All provide the necessary resources and contact information if you or someone you know may have a gambling problem. The minimum age is 18 for horse racing betting in most states, but it is 21 in some states.             Responsible gambling resources include the National Council for Problem Gambling (NCPG) and Gamblers Anonymous. Be smart. Bet smart. Wager responsibly. Those in need of help can also call or text 1-800-GAMBLER (1-800-426-2537). Help is available 24 hours a day and seven days a week.               FAQ    How to bet on horse racing?  There are several ways to bet on horse racing. The most common methods are through horse racing betting apps like TwinSpires, FanDuel Racing, and DraftKings Horse. Users can bet on a variety of outcomes, with the most common wager coming on which horse will win the given race outright.    How to bet on horse racing online?  Online horse racing betting is widely accessible. TwinSpires, DraftKings Horse, and FanDuel Racing all provide users with a huge array of betting options on all major races.    What is a box bet in horse racing?  A box bet in horse racing involves picking the finishing order of the horses. Wagerers can choose the order of the first two, three, four, or five finishers, with the return on their bet increasing with every additional horse they include in their wager. If a bettor chooses three horses for a box bet, they do not need to finish in an exact order. If they make up the top three, the bet is successful.    What is a show bet in horse racing?  A show bet is a wager on a specific horse to finish among the top three horses in a given race. Show bets are extremely common wagers that offer less risk and smaller payouts.    What is a key box bet in horse racing?  A key box bet, unsurprisingly, functions similarly to a box bet. A bettor can select a "key" horse that they believe will finish in an exact position while rounding out the rest of the box in the same fashion as a regular box bet. For example, a bettor could select Horse A to finish first while picking Horses C, B, and D to round out the top four. However, if Horse A does not finish first, the bet loses.

        On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts made two major moves towards a rebuild with the trades of offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner. Nelson's trade came first, with Indy sending him to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks for a third-round pick and a future fifth-round pick.Their second big news of the day was Indianapolis trading Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, according to ESPN. Buckner will now have a second stint with the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.These Colts trades come just about a week after firing general manager Chris Ballard. Sitting at 2-4 at the time of the firing, and 2-5 now, Indy is clearly beginning their much-needed rebuild and making those big changes along with it. 
        
            
                Quenton Nelson trade grades: Seahawks add eight-time Pro Bowler, while Colts look to sell pieces
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Niners are the opposite of a rebuild, with sights set on the playoffs and beyond. They now added a reliable defensive big man who can help get them there.
Both sides can take many positives from the deal, with the edge going to the Niners. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Colts: B+The Colts situation, sitting at 2-5, firing their GM and needing to rebuild, certainly doesn't earn a B+, but this trade does. Freeing up cap space and getting the most value for their players while they can is a smart move on their part.If the Colts kept Buckner and he signed with another team this offseason, the highest compensatory draft pick they could've received for him was a fifth-rounder. The 11-year veteran was likely going elsewhere at the end of the year anyway, emphasizing recently that at this stage in his career he wants to play winning football. 
After their loss to the Tennessee Titans, who went into the contest without a win, in Week 6, Buckner said he was "frustrated" and added, "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year." He now gets to play meaningful football, and the Colts get the most value in return. Instead of a 2028 fifth-round pick, they now have a 2027 fourth-round pick. Tuesday's moves have cleared over $17.7 million in salary cap space and added three draft picks. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    49ers: AThe 49ers' time to win is now, which means all chips are in. The Niners are one of the NFC's and the NFL's best teams at 6-1. Despite an abundance of injuries, they've managed to put on solid performances.Adding some security on the defensive line gives the team that added assurance, along with a veteran presence, someone with postseason experience and someone they know. Defensive tackles C.J. West and Alfred Collins are on IR, so the Niners were already in the market to cushion that position. Buckner has already spent multiple seasons with the team, so he not only knows the front office and schemes and has played with some of these guys before, but he will also have that extra fire that comes from a reunion with a former team.
Not to mention, his new/former teammates are happy:
This season, Buckner has 31 combined tackles, four sacks and three pass breakups in seven starts. In 158 games, including 153 starts, he has 683 combined tackles, including 101 for a loss, 75.5 sacks, 31 pass deflections, nine forced fumbles, 11 fumble recoveries, nine forced fumbles and two touchdowns.When the Niners do make that playoff push, if they do as they are expected and make it to the postseason, Buckner will know that song and dance. He was there when the 49ers made a Super Bowl run, losing to the Kansas City Chiefs to end the 2019 season. He started all three playoff games that season, finishing with 12 combined tackles, four quarterback hits, 2.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery,

Seattle shores up protection for Sam Darnold with an eight-time Pro Bowler, while Indianapolis opens the door to sell more
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks made a splashy move ahead of the trade deadline, as they acquired former Indianapolis Colts eight-time Pro Bowl offensive guard Quenton Nelson for a third-round pick and a future fifth-round pick. The 2-5 Colts were thought to be sellers ahead of the trade deadline, having already fired general manager Chris Ballard. Interim general manager Ed Dodds has a relationship with Seahawks general manager John Schneider, as he worked in Seattle from 2007-2016 as a scout and senior personnel executive. The Colts have a couple of intriguing trade pieces on expiring deals, including Nelson, who now finds himself on a contender. According to The Ringer, Seattle will pay the remaining $9.78 million on Nelson's deal. The former No. 6 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame has long been regarded as one of the best offensive guards in the NFL, having earned eight straight Pro Bowl nods and three First Team All-Pro selections from 2018-2020. Not only is Nelson effective at protecting quarterbacks from interior pass rushers, but he's also incredibly durable, having not missed a game since the 2021 season. Let's attempt to grade this massive trade.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seahawks: AIn seven games played this season, Nelson has allowed six pressures and zero sacks from his left guard spot, according to TruMedia. The Seahawks' offensive line has struggled in 2026, especially on the interior, where they've allowed the highest pressure rate in the NFL, per CBS Sports Research. While Sam Darnold was kept clean on Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs, he was hit 17 times and sacked five times in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos. 
PFF ranked Seattle's offensive line as the No. 9 unit entering Week 7, pointing out that the right side was a weak spot. With the addition of Nelson, the Seahawks will likely move former first-round pick Grey Zabel to right guard, per ESPN.It's true that Nelson could be playing for another team in 2027, but the Seahawks have traded for expiring deals before and re-signed those players. It happened just last year with wide receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed. Seahawks' notable midseason trade acquisitions over the past four seasonsYearPlayer acquired2023DT Leonard Williams2024LB Ernest Jones IV2025 WR Rashid Shaheed2026OG Quenton NelsonPlus, the compensation Seattle gave up for a top offensive guard makes this an "A" grade. Adam Schefter points out that the Seahawks should have five compensatory picks in this upcoming draft after losing Kenneth Walker III, Tariq Woolen, Coby Bryant and Boye Mafe in free agency. They also get a third-round pick after former assistant general manager Nolan Teasley was hired to be the new GM of the Minnesota Vikings. Seattle has capital to utilize, and this looks like a wise investment. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Colts: C+It's hard for the Colts to "win" this kind of trade. Not only are they selling off elite talent at a discount, but a move like this also signals that the Colts' 2026 season is over. They aren't the sleeper in the AFC South fans hoped they would be, and it just opens the door for other players like Jonathan Taylor or DeForest Buckner to be moved. Remember, the Colts do not own their 2027 first-round pick after sending it to the New York Jets for Sauce Gardner last year. One question I have is if the Colts waited two more weeks to trade Nelson, could they have fetched a better package? We'll never know. ESPN reports the Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles all showed interest in Nelson prior to Tuesday.

body:
It's been a struggle for Adebayo to find space to operate next to Antetokounmpo as Miami is off to an 0-4 start
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Miami Heat are off to a dreadful start to the 2026-27 season, dropping their first four games after a 113-109 loss on Monday night to the Dallas Mavericks. It's not the start anyone in Miami envisioned after trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo this summer, and all of the worst fears about the Heat's roster and a potentially clunky offensive fit between Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have already come to fruition in the first week of the season. Adebayo is off to the worst start to a season in his career since becoming a full-time starter, averaging 11.8 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists per game on 40.0/16.7/61.5 shooting splits -- all of which would represent career-low shooting marks. A four-game sample is not enough to entirely write off the partnership, but it has been about the worst-case scenario for how those two stars can work off of each other. Adebayo said outside critics are making him out to be "the scapegoat" of Miami's early-season struggles, but with a roster already thin on offensive talent, the Heat's second star struggling this badly is going to bring quite the spotlight. 

        
            
                Winners and losers of NBA's first week: Giannis' Heat are ice cold, OKC injuries and new-look wonders
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Davion Mitchell, the team's starting point guard, was asked about Adebayo's struggles after Monday's loss to Dallas and succinctly explained why it's a tough fit alongside Antetokounmpo. "I think I got to do a better job of not letting [Adebayo] get lost in the game," Mitchell said, via ESPN. "He got to be more aggressive. I think that he will. He's still trying to figure it out because I said this before -- I think him and Giannis play in the same spaces, and then when Giannis is on the floor, he's on the floor. He can't be in those spaces, and but it's something to get used to."That was always the concern with that partnership, and as Mitchell noted, if it's a matter of Adebayo or Antetokounmpo being in his preferred spot, it's almost always going to be Antetokounmpo getting his way. The problem is that it puts Adebayo in spots where he's uncomfortable. And even when he is getting touches in his best spots, the spacing is off because Antetokounmpo also wants to get to the paint. 
Perhaps the most worrisome part of this for Adebayo is that Antetokounmpo's history tells us he's not going to change for the betterment of his co-star. Antetokounmpo's partnership with Damian Lillard made it abundantly clear that he's not the type to adjust his game tremendously to make for a better fit with a star, as he didn't want to be part of a pick-and-roll-heavy two-man game with Lillard that could've made the Bucks' offense special. That means there's little reason to expect Antetokounmpo to suddenly recognize he and Adebayo want to play in similar spots and to yield that position to Adebayo more often. If that's the case, the onus gets put on Adebayo to completely alter his game 10 years into his NBA career. So far, that reinvention isn't going very well, as his 3-point shot has not fallen and he's struggling to get opportunities inside -- his 6.8 2-point attempts per game are by far his lowest since becoming a starter in his third season. 
As Mitchell notes, some of it comes down to Adebayo being more aggressive, but it's harder to do so when you aren't in comfortable spots. With Antetokounmpo unlikely to change his style to help Adebayo adapt, it's going to be up to Adebayo to sink or swim in this new partnership.

body:
Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline is exactly two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr. heading to the Cowboys, Marvin Harrison Jr. heading to the Texans and Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks, and we could see several more over the next 14 days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment. With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top 10 situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all.So without further ado, here's the list...The Eagles 
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles (Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.  
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith, whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge. Dallas Goedert, meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price. The Colts 
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs. The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away. 
The Titans 
It would be pretty surprising if Jeffery Simmons were dealt away, considering he recently signed a three-year, $105.8 million contract extension that made him the highest-paid defensive tackle in the NFL. But the Titans are going nowhere fast, and Simmons is by far their best asset if they want to kick-start yet another rebuild, which seems to be in the offing. Tennessee would take on a bunch of dead money by dealing him, but it might be worth it if they can get as much draft capital as he's worth. Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team.  Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back. 
Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help. The Chargers 
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick. Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now. 
Derwin James, like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for. Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around. The Cardinals 
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.  
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team. Jacoby Brissett is clearly not the long-term answer under center for the Cardinals, and they might turn to Carson Beck sooner rather than later so they can see what they have in the third-round pick before making a decision on whether to select a quarterback in next year's draft. That makes Brissett expendable, and some team looking for a quality backup or fill-in for an injured starter could be interested in his services. The Dolphins 
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler, though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed). 
Jordyn Brooks, like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks under team control for multiple years. With the emergence of rookie Jacob Rodriguez and Brooks having recently turned 29 years old, they could look to deal him for a pretty sizable return. Brian Thomas Jr.  
Brian Thomas Jr. has pretty clearly fallen out of favor in Jacksonville. In the Jaguars' last game, he didn't play a single second-half snap. Rookie Josh Cameron is playing ahead of him, and now it seems that two-way star Travis Hunter might be as well. But Thomas has more of a track record of high-level production than did Marvin Harrison Jr., and MHJ fetched a second-round pick via trade. If the Jaguars could get that type of return, they should be very interested, and teams should be interested in acquiring him as well, considering what he did as a rookie (albeit maybe not for quite that high a price, considering what he's done this year and last).Daron Payne 
The Commanders are going nowhere and Daron Payne is in the final year of his contract. His $16.4 million base salary is high but not prohibitive to a trade. He's still a quality run defender, even if he doesn't give you that much in the way of pass-rush juice these days. The Commies would be wise to get something for him before he leaves in free agency next offseason. 
Will McDonald IV 
Will McDonald IV has seen his snap rate cut from 66% down to 46% this season after the arrival of David Bailey in the draft. But he had 10.5 and 8 sacks over the last two seasons, and has shown he can be a productive pass rusher. The Jets just lost to the aforementioned Dolphins, so it's not like they're really going to compete for anything this year. McDonald had his fifth-year option picked up for next season, but he's still affordable. Kirk Cousins 
Klint Kubiak is already getting questions about when he's going to turn the reins over to Fernando Mendoza, which means Kirk Cousins' time under center is likely coming to an end fairly soon. Like Brissett, he could be valuable to a team looking for either a quality backup or a fill-in starter for the rest of the season. The Raiders might prefer to just keep him around and have him mentor Mendoza for the rest of the year, though. Jauan Jennings
Jauan Jennings has so far been entirely uninvolved in the Vikings' offense. It would be surprising to see the league's last remanining unbeaten team make a trade where the give away an asset instead of acquire one, but given Jennings' lack of role and the number of teams in need of wide receiver help, this is certainly a situation worth monitoring.

        Utah Jazz forward Jaren Jackson Jr. suffered a torn MCL in his right knee on Monday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, the team announced Tuesday. Jackson's injury, which came in the first quarter of Monday's loss to the Memphis Grizzlies when Ty Jerome fell into his knee, will not require surgery, according to ESPN.That wasn't the only front-court injury Utah sustained in the loss, as Lauri Markkanen injured his wrist attempting to get around a screen in the first quarter. The team said Tuesday that Markkanen is considered day-to-day. Neither returned to the game as they played just 16 combined minutes in the defeat.Even if Markkanen avoids serious injury, Jackson's absence puts the Jazz in an enormously difficult situation, considering the direction their offseason took. After a contract standoff with former starting center Walker Kessler, the Jazz elected to sign-and-trade him to the Los Angeles Lakers for two first-round picks and two first-round swaps. It's early, but Kessler has been spectacular for the Lakers, and his absence left the Jazz without a long-term option at center. Short-term starter Jusuf Nurkić is also injured, and now, the Jazz are without Jackson, their rim-protecting power forward.
Utah has spent the bulk of the past four seasons tanking. This season carried at least Play-In expectations after the emergence of Keyonte George last year and with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick Darryn Peterson. Those goals are obviously not out of reach even with Jackson injured, but a 1-3 start coupled with everything they've lost in the front-court certainly leaves Utah behind the eight ball early on. The Jazz already rank No. 25 in the NBA defensively, and while their rebounding has surprised early in the season, it is a clear weakness on paper.The Jazz have the ammunition to make a sizable trade if they want to. That was one of the benefits of trading Kessler. But teams are rarely eager to give away valuable veterans early in seasons, and roughly 29% of all NBA players are not currently eligible for trades because of contracts they signed during the offseason. 
For now, Utah will probably have to rely on incumbent big men like Jaxson Hayes, Mo Bamba and Kyle Filipowski while they await the return of at least Nurkić and then, eventually, Jackson.
